title: Ordinary balanced-tensor comparison for the embedded first quotient
statement: Fix prime ell, finite intermediate field E of PadicAlgCl ell, a maximal-ideal generator pi in its integers, and a Noetherian scheme X. Suppose completedResidue ell E pi 0 is finite and discrete. With phi = scalarMap ell E X, q = residueMap ell E pi X, e = finiteScalarMap X (completedResidue ell E pi 0), and p = (integralModelReductionMap X ell E pi 1).hom, there is a natural isomorphism (Mod.comap phi followed by ordinary scalar extension along q and then e) isomorphic to ordinary scalar extension along p. All maps are those of [def-sfb-embedded-finite-coefficient-realization]; this is a statement about ordinary module categories, with no derived categories or resolutions.

proof.text: Naturality of constantToContinuous for the quotient ring homomorphism, followed by additive forgetting and upperStarFromPoint, gives the equality scalarMap followed by the specified continuous first reduction = residueMap followed by finiteScalarMap. The latter specified finite scalar map is an isomorphism.

On the coefficient-sized small site, use the completion diagram and flat_and_quotients at exponent one to obtain sectionwise surjectivity of the actual constant quotient. Use the proved residue-sections helper for a common generator of the two section kernels. Postcomposition by the specified finite scalar isomorphism preserves the constant kernel and surjectivity. Perform these section arguments for general ring sheaves before specialization to avoid unfolding the large reconstructed coefficient objects. Ideal.map_span identifies the continuous kernel with the ideal generated by scalar images of the constant kernel.

Apply the existing quotientTensorIso_exists in ConstantCompletion to the actual small-site maps, taking the constant quotient followed by the finite scalar map as the common target quotient. Its quotientTensorAdjunction proves that restriction followed by ordinary tensor extension is left adjoint to continuous quotient restriction: a restriction-linear map into a quotient module is linear over the continuous coefficients, since their kernel is generated by images of the constant kernel. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives the ordinary comparison.

Transport the ordinary comparison back through smallModules. The proved smallModulesEquivalence and smallRestrictionIso helpers identify module categories and restriction. Taking the inverse mate of this restriction isomorphism through the ordinary tensor adjunction gives smallExtensionIso; mates through equivalences are invertible. Cancel the fully faithful smallModules functor from the resulting natural isomorphism, then use extendScalarsComp and the functor associator to recover the stated parenthesized composite. Only the ordinary transport helpers of the embedded-completion and internal-section-adjunction modules are used; neither derived completion nor a resolution is invoked.

lean.statement:
theorem embeddedFirstReductionOrdinary
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ)
    (π : PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E.1)
    (hπ : Ideal.span {π} = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E.1))
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    [Finite (completedResidue ℓ E π 0)] [DiscreteTopology (completedResidue ℓ E π 0)] :
    Nonempty ((Mod.comap (scalarMap ℓ E X) ⋙ Mod.extendScalars (residueMap ℓ E π X)) ⋙
      Mod.extendScalars (finiteScalarMap X (completedResidue ℓ E π 0)) ≅
        Mod.extendScalars (integralModelReductionMap X ℓ E π 1).hom)
